newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Judge allows YPF share sale after it pays deposit.
newsitem.headline: Judge allows YPF share sale after it pays deposit.

text.p: An Argentine judge has amended an earlier ruling and allowed the planned sale of 10 percent of shares in oil firm YPF to proceed, after YPF made a deposit of $400,000 in guarantees, state-run Telam news agency said.
"We accept that decision that allows the sale of the shares," under Secretary for Banks Francisco Susmel was quoted by Telam as saying late Tuesday.
"But we will challenge the one by which the judge replaces his earlier ban on (the shares) transaction for an embargo of $400,000 YPF has deposited."
Telam said Susmel moved to contact Salomon Brothers to inform them to go ahead and open Wednesday bids received in the United States Monday and Tuesday.

Banco Comafi and Merchant Bankers Asociados, an Argentine affiliate of Salomon Brothers Inc, as well as Salomon Brothers in New York, had been accepting bids for the shares since 1700 local time Monday.
The cut-off price for the auction of the shares should have been announced at 1015 local time/1315 GMT Tuesday.
Judge Enrique Arias Gibert Monday ordered the suspension of the sale following a complaint by 11 former YPF workers, but Tuesday he allowed the sale after YPF made the $400,000 deposit.
Judicial sources told Reuters many other former YPF employees may make similar claims in other courts.

Argentina's government authorized the sale of the 33.5 million Class C YPF shares in the hands of the company's employees --10 percent of the firm's stock -- by a decree issued last Friday. The shares are to be auctioned simultaneously in New York and Buenos Aires.
The government owns another 20 percent of the firm but says it has no immediate plans to sell.
Proceeds from the sale are expected to be around $1.1 billion. From that amount, employees owe the government $650 million.
